reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-29: Portfolio holding 56% cash vs 28% mandate creates 4% APY drag on $1B+ notional ($29.8M annual cost). Position underweights require deployment into mandated allocations to restore stated strategy: SOXL from 11% to 18% (semis consolidation mandate target), IWM from 11% to 18% (small-cap recovery mandate target), dividend cluster from 13% to 22% (aristocrat defensive base), UPRO from 6.11% to 10% (leveraged tech exposure), TLT short from 2.44% to 4% (rate hedge). NVIDIA's exceptional earnings ($96.22B revenue beat 4.82%, 70% FY2028 growth guidance, $1T order book through 2027) validates semiconductor structural case; semis rallied 3-8.7% on results, SOXL +52% YTD. Small-cap momentum intact: Russell 2000 +22-23% YTD outperforming S&P 500 by 9.1pp at 34.5% valuation discount. Dividend aristocrats performing: SCHD +20% YTD, JNJ/PG/MCD all maintaining yield and growth. Rates elevated at 4.72% 10-year and 5.26% 30-year (inflation-driven, highest since June 2007) supports TLT short hedge. Deployment eliminates cash drag and aligns portfolio with stated mandate.
research_notes: Research through 2026-08-28 shows transformative developments: NVIDIA's Q2 earnings ($96.22B revenue, beat by 4.82%) with extraordinary 70% FY2028 guidance and $1 trillion order book for 2026-2027 validate semiconductor structural tailwinds; semis rallied 3-8.7% on results. Russell 2000 continues strong performance at +22-23% YTD, outperforming S&P 500 by 9.1pp, with small-caps still trading 34.5% discount to large-cap multiples. Interest rate environment remains elevated (10-year at 4.72%, 30-year at 5.26% highest since June 2007) driven by inflation concerns and potential Fed rate increase, supporting long-duration bond shorts. Dividend aristocrats performing solidly: SCHD +20% YTD, JNJ 2.17% yield with 64-year history, PG 2.96% yield with 70-year streak. Round 2 carrying excess cash (56% vs 28% mandate) creating cost drag; rebalancing deploys capital into outperforming sectors aligned with stated mandate. Round 3's defensive value thesis continues working (+1.70% P&L), with tactical shorts serving portfolio insurance role despite recent sector strength.
